    AI Overview
    The Illinois House of Representatives is the lower chamber of the Illinois General Assembly, established in 1818, which meets in Springfield. The 104th General Assembly consists of 118 members, currently with 78 Democrats and 40 Republicans. Members serve two-year terms with no term limits. 
    Leadership (104th General Assembly): 
    • Majority Leader: Robyn Gabel (Democratic)
    • Minority Leader: Not explicitly named, but key GOP leaders include Ryan Spain, Norine Hammond, and Patrick Windhorst.
    • Speaker:
      The Speaker is elected by the House membership.
       
    Key Functions and Recent Action: 
    • Legislation: The House passes legislation on issues such as budget, education, healthcare, and criminal justice, with over 100 bills passed recently.
    • Recent Activity: Recent focus includes abortion coverage, detention centers, rental fee limits, voter registration, and curbing gun violence.
    • Committees: The House utilizes various committees for reviewing legislation. 
    Election and Qualifications: 
    • Members are elected every two years in general elections.
    • They must be a United States citizen, at least 21 years old, and a resident of their district for at least two years prior to election. 
    Key representatives include Brad Halbrook (107th District), Regan Deering, Carol Ammons, and Jaime M. Andrade, Jr.

    Structure. What is the organizational structure of the Illinois House of Representatives?
    About this result
    Feedback
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    The Illinois House of Representatives is structured as a 118-member legislative body within the bicameral Illinois General Assembly, with each member elected from a single-member district for a two-year term. The House is led by an elected Speaker, supported by majority and minority leaders, and operates through committees to pass legislation. 
    Key Aspects of the Organizational Structure
    • Composition: 118 Representatives, elected from 118 separate districts. 
    • Leadership: The Speaker of the House is elected by the full membership, typically from the majority party. 
    • Majority/Minority Leadership: Includes a Majority Leader, Minority Leader, and whips who manage party strategy and voting. 
    • Committees: The Speaker appoints all chairs, co-chairs, and vice-chairs, as well as majority caucus members, while the Minority Leader appoints minority caucus members to committees. 
    • Sessions: Convenes annually on the second Wednesday in January in Springfield. 
    Usage Examples of the Structure
    • Passage of Laws:
      Legislation requires a majority vote in the House, and upon gaining the assent of the Governor, it becomes law. 
    • Committee Work:
      Bills are assigned to committees for review, hearings, and modifications before reaching the floor. 
    • Redistricting:
      The House holds the power to redraw its own district boundaries every 10 years, often with leadership control. 
    Synonyms/Related Terminology
    • Illinois General Assembly (ILGA): The overarching legislative body, which includes the House and Senate. 
    • Lower House: Commonly used to refer to the House of Representatives. 
    • State Representatives: Members of the House. 
    • Caucus: Party groups within the House (e.g., Democratic Caucus, Republican Caucus). 
    The structure of the House is designed to ensure legislative power is concentrated in a large, frequently elected body (two-year terms) to ensure responsiveness to constituent needs.

      AI Overview
      The 104th Illinois General Assembly (2025–2027) consists of 118 members, currently with a Democratic supermajority (78 Democrats, 40 Republicans). Emanuel "Chris" Welch (D-Hillside) serves as Speaker of the House, and Tony McCombie (R-Savanna) serves as Minority Leader. 
      Key Leadership and Members of the 104th General Assembly: 
      • Speaker: Emanuel "Chris" Welch (D-7th District)
      • Minority Leader: Tony McCombie (R-71st District)
      • Assistant Majority Leader: Dagmara Avelar (D-85th District)
      • Other Notable Members: Carol Ammons (103rd), Jaime M. Andrade, Jr. (40th), Harry Benton (97th), Rick Ryan (36th).
      Key Facts about the House: 
      • Composition: 118 members, each elected from single-member districts.
      • Supermajority: The Democratic Party holds a majority in the House.
      • Function: Members were inaugurated in January 2025.
      For a complete, interactive list of current members, including contact information and district maps, the official Illinois General Assembly website is the primary source.

        AI Overview
        Members of the Illinois House of Representatives are elected to two-year terms. There are 118 representatives, each representing a specific district and elected in every even-numbered year. There are no term limits for members of the Illinois House of Representatives. 
        Key details regarding the term length include:
        • Term Duration: 2 years. 
        • Election Cycle: All 118 seats are up for election every two years. 
        • Term Limits: There are no term limits for Illinois House members. 
        • Leader Limits: While members have no term limits, House rules create limits for leadership positions, such as speaker and minority leader. 
        This information pertains to the Illinois State House of Representatives, not the U.S. House of Representatives.

          Qualifications. What are the qualifications to be a member of the Illinois House of Representatives?
          About this result
          Feedback
          An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
          AI Overview
          To be a member of the Illinois House of Representatives (state-level), you must be a U.S. citizen, at least 21 years old, and a resident of your district for the two years preceding the election or appointment. You must also file nomination papers, including a statement of candidacy and petition signatures. 
          Key Qualifications for the Illinois House of Representatives:
          • Age: Minimum 21 years old. 
          • Citizenship: Must be a United States citizen. 
          • Residency: Must be a resident of the district you wish to represent for at least two years immediately preceding the election or appointment. 
          • Other Requirements: Candidates must file nomination papers, which include a statement of candidacy, a statement of economic interests, and petition signatures to get on the ballot. 
          • Restrictions: You cannot have been convicted of a felony, bribery, perjury, or other infamous crimes. 
          Usage Examples and Procedures: 
          • Filing Petitions: Candidates for the Illinois House must gather valid signatures from registered voters in their district.
          • Statement of Candidacy: This document confirms you meet all legal qualifications for the office.
          • Statement of Economic Interest: A required filing detailing financial interests to ensure transparency.
          Synonyms/Related Terms for Qualifications: Eligibility requirements, Candidate requirements, Legislative eligibility criteria, Ballot access requirements, and Constitutional qualifications.
          Note: The results indicate a distinction between the Illinois House of Representatives (State) and the U.S. House of Representatives from Illinois. The requirements above are for the Illinois General Assembly (State Legislature).

            Role. What is the role of the Illinois House of Representatives?
            About this result
            Feedback
            An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
            AI Overview
            The Illinois House of Representatives is the lower chamber of the Illinois General Assembly, responsible for creating state laws, establishing the state budget, and representing constituents. Comprised of 118 elected members serving two-year terms, it passes legislation, sets tax levels, and holds the power to impeach state officials. 
            Key roles of the Illinois House include:
            • Legislation: Proposing, debating, and passing bills on public policy matters. 
            • Budgeting: Setting state spending levels and controlling tax policy. 
            • Oversight: Reviewing government administration and exercising the power to impeach officials. 
            • Checks and Balances: Voting to uphold or override vetoes from the Governor. 
            • Representation: Serving citizens by acting on issues like property taxes, education, and social services. 
            The House serves as part of the legislative branch alongside the Illinois Senate to make laws in Springfield.
